note: A patch of colour change centred on the summit craters, under one cycle. On a 3,300 m cone this could be partly water vapour that varies with height; Sentinel-1 pairs from late Aug-early Sep show summit rings that a weather model only partly removes. Treat as possible, not proven, ground motion.

what: Each full cycle of colour is about 12 cm of ground motion toward or away from the satellite (L-band, 24 cm wavelength).
credit: Contains NISAR data (NASA/ISRO) processed by COMET LiCSAR; LiCSAR uses JASMIN, the UK's collaborative data analysis environment (http://jasmin.ac.uk). Re-coloured and cropped by Bluish Void.
licence: LiCSAR products: Open Government Licence v3.0 (CEDA catalogue entry for LiCSAR); that entry describes the Sentinel-1 products, its coverage of COMET's NISAR folder is not stated. Underlying NISAR data are NASA open data.
note: Very coherent L-band picture of the whole cone; a local colour change on the east side of the crater lake (Segara Anak, where the young Barujari cone sits) stands out. Only one NISAR geometry covers it here, so atmosphere cannot be ruled out. Pair is older than 60 days (ended 14 Aug).

what: Each full cycle of colour is about 2.8 cm of change in the radar's path length toward or away from the satellite (C-band, 5.5 cm wavelength).
credit: LiCSAR contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026 analysed by the Centre for the Observation and Modelling of Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Tectonics (COMET). LiCSAR uses JASMIN, the UK's collaborative data analysis environment (http://jasmin.ac.uk). Re-coloured and cropped by Bluish Void.
licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 (CEDA catalogue: LiCSAR interferometry products, Lazecky & Maghsoudi 2022)
note: NOT ground motion. These perfect bullseye rings are water vapour: they follow the mountain's height, vanish in a 6-day pair, and disappear when LiCSAR's own GACOS weather-model delay is subtracted. Kept as the honest counter-example.
